title: The Days School Isn't an Option

body.en: Abena is fourteen and usually a strong student. But every time the borehole near her house dries up, fetching water becomes her job before school — and some mornings, the queue is so long she misses her first two classes. During the last flood, the road to her school was impassable for six days straight. Her teachers don't always know why she's behind; they just see the missed days. Abena isn't struggling with the material. She's struggling with a climate that keeps deciding, without asking her, whether today is a day she gets to go to school at all.

followUpQuestion: What are the two different climate events in Abena's story that each disrupted her schooling, and how?
